utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Margetts, are you ready to continue the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to remind you, Mr. Savkic, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony; that is that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but truth. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Margetts: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, when we concluded on Friday, we were going through your various positions that you held between 1991 and 1995, and you had provided details in respect of the positions you held in the party and the positions you've held in government, and you were commencing with your answer in relation to the positions that you held in the military, and if my memory serves me correctly, you'd reached September 1992, and so I invite you to continue with the description of the positions that you held, the units you were involved with in the military until the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived by September, and I said that after the commander for the defence of the mine, I returned and was the person in charge of engineering until the 1st of November, 1992, when I took over the 1st Infantry Battalion, and as commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion, I was at that post until the 1st of November, 1993, when I became the president of the Municipal Assembly, and after that I was no longer part of the military formations. I would just like to make an addition regarding the party. I remembered that I did not say that from the period 2001. Perhaps I did say it, but I don't think that I did, that from 2001 until 2005, I was member of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party. And also, if you allow me, I remember I did express reserves at the time, but when I was asked by the Defence counsel, who were the councillors or deputies who left with Hodzic, I mentioned Atif Ceric. I don't rule out the possibility that he was a deputy, but I think that the person that we talked about, the shopkeeper, was Hasan Dzindo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savkic. There's just one area I'm not entirely clear on, and that is that your record shows that you were engaged in war service from the 6th of April, 1992. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber precisely what unit you were involved in from the 6th of April, 1992, until the transformation of the TO into the Infantry Brigade subordinated to the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was from the 6th of April that I was in any military unit. What I said was that our military booklets had either the date 4th of April or the 6th of April written down in them. There is a reason why this date was put in our booklets. I said that in that period, later, other than -- first of all, I'm thinking of March -- no, May. Other than carrying out my functions in my company, I was also carrying out the work regarding the engineering provisions in relation to the mine at the staff or the command of this unit of the Territorial Defence or, rather, that battalion. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savkic. I'd now like to move to your election -- or not your election but your appointment as a deputy in the Republika Srpska Assembly. I have a copy of the attendance records of the Assembly for the period from May 1992 through to the period October 1993, and I'd like to present those to you. They're contained in tab 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your list it appears as having no number yet, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If that could receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 20, Your Honours, will be P1054.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, if you could look at the document before you, you'll see that at the top of the table there is a reference which states -- which explains what the table represents, and that is it says: "The numbers on the right-hand side indicate the number of the sessions from which the deputy was absent." Can you please look at number 74, which is your name, and you'll see that there listed at number 74 are the sessions that you did not attend in the period May 1992 through to October 1993. Mr. Savkic, do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy of this report?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have number 74 on my list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I think if you turn over the page, twice, in fact. Apologies for that. It's broken up due to the stamp which authenticates this as an original document.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states here that I did not attend the 16th, 20th, 23rd, 24th, 34th, the 3rd part, and the 35th sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any reason to dispute the accuracy of this record?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the dates of these sessions right now. I should know the dates. I don't know specifically what you mean. I don't see the dates when these sessions were held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the dates are not contained there. I can assist you in some respects, and that is to say as follows: The 16th session which it's listed that you did not attend was a session on the 12th of May, 1992, held in Banja Luka. The next session which these records record you did attend was the 17th session, which was held at the Bistrica hotel in Jahorina. Is that consistent with your memory that that was the first session you attended?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The date for that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date of that session was the 24th to the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that the session that adopted that decision - this was in May - all I know is that I was given that mandate then. I was not at that session, definitely, and I know that the first session that I did attend was in September or October, but I know that the first session that I attended was, as far as I can remember, held in Prijedor. I cannot recall attending any other sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Savkic, the session that you were nominated as the deputy to replace Mr. Zekic was in fact this session, the 17th session of the 24th to 26th July, 1992, at the Bistrica hotel, Jahorina. Were you present on the day that your nomination to replace Mr. Zekic was on the agenda of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's the session, then I definitely did not attend it. If that's the one held at Bistrica, then I definitely did not attend. I thought that that was the May session. But, no, if you say that this was held at Bistrica, meaning later, then I definitely did not attend it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll move on. If you could close the exhibits before you. Now, you told the Trial Chamber that you lived all your life in Milici, and in fact you lived in the village of Dubnica. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was born in Dubnica. I lived my whole life in Milici, except for 1983, when I had an apartment as a professor. From 1983 until the 14th of June, 1994, when I moved to the Boksit Company. And at the same time, I actually offered my thanks for the school apartment. So this was a period of one year. And even then I didn't sleep, because one of my colleagues slept there because I was sleeping at my parents' in Dubnicki Most, or Dubnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your friend Rade Bjelanovic, he was from the village of Gornji Zalukovik; correct? Sorry, the witness is indicating that he didn't receive a translation. I will repeat the question, Mr. Savkic. Your friend Rade Bjelanovic, he was from the village of Gornji Zalukovik; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I'm -- I'm -- Radomir Bjelanovic was born in Gornji Zalukovik, and he lived for most of his life in Vlasenica. Also, sometime in the 1980s, he was given an apartment in Milici. However, then - I mean when he was in Vlasenica and over there - he was an engineer in the same company that I worked at, and I've already said we were good friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Savkic, if we could move on to the Crisis Staff of Milici, that's the Serb Crisis Staff of Milici. You mentioned in your evidence-in-chief that that was disbanded on the 30th of May, 1992, and you also gave evidence that the Muslims were forming Crisis Staffs at the time that you had the Municipal Assembly meeting on the 14th of April, 1992. When was the Serb Crisis Staff formed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In your question, something is obviously not quite right. You're talking about the Serb Crisis Staff in Milici, and you're talking about the session on the 14th of April in Vlasenica. I don't know if the interpretation was correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in that case, let me be clear and not confound the issue. The first thing I was saying was that you told the Trial Chamber that on the 14th of April, 1992, when you had the Municipal Assembly meeting in Vlasenica, that the Muslims were not present, and in fact they were forming Crisis Staffs. That's the first point. The second point is this: That in your evidence-in-chief you said that the Milici Crisis Staff was disbanded on the 30th of May, 1992. So what I'd like you now to tell the Trial Chamber - and you only need to give the date - when was the Milici Crisis Staff formed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, I don't know, either because the translation was incorrect or -- I don't know, but in the transcript it will state clearly at the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, on the 14th of April or the 16th of April, it doesn't matter, I said was attended by deputies of Muslim ethnicity. His Honour the Presiding Judge asked me how many of such deputies were there. I said either three to five at least, up to 15 the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the mistake is mine. What I have said is Muslims were not present. I should have said a number of the Muslim representatives were not present. But putting that aside and putting aside the background I've tried to give you to orient your answer, can you just then answer this question, just this simple question: When was the Crisis Staff of Milici formed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Milici Crisis Staff was never formed, as far as I know. As far as I know, the Crisis Staff in Milici was never formed. The Municipal Assembly was formed. It was constituted, as well as the Executive Board. That was also established. That's what I said. This can be found in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also talked about the Serbian municipality of Milici. I take it that a statute was adopted establishing the Milici municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the statute probably was adopted. That's your assumption. But that's something that should be put to the Milici president of the Municipal Assembly, who is a person, and his first and last name is known. I can tell you what his first and last name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Savkic, you referred to the protocol establishing the Milici municipality. When was the Milici municipality first proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Milici municipality. I can't remember the date it was proclaimed, but from 1945 until 1958, the Milici municipality existed. Then it was abolished and joined with the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Savkic. I'm -- I'm intending to refer to the Milici municipality that's been the subject of your evidence and was the subject of the protocol signed on the 11th of April, 1992. When was that Milici municipality proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Milici municipality, once the joint Assembly session was held in Vlasenica, was proclaimed then. However, all the preparations regarding its actual existence - I mean that's probably when the statute that you mention was adopted - anyway, all of this was carried out in late March. I think that it was the 31st of March, actually. I'm not sure, but I think that all this was done on the 31st of March. It was constituted, then the potential deputies were taken into consideration, how many of them, and how it can be constituted also was looked at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to the specific date, the 31st of March. Why has that date come to your mind? Do you have any documents in mind that relate to the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have these documents here now, but in the archives of the Municipal Assembly of Milici I believe the document exists.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you are sort of obstructing the microphone with the thing your papers are lying on. So could you turn on the other microphone or do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I apologise for that. I have now turned on both microphones to my left and my right. I hope that is of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, now the sound comes back on the other microphone, so three is too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Okay. If I try two, does that work or have we got it echoing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, up to the moment that we hear the whistle in our earphones. Is it sufficient for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The left one is actually better. If you can switch that one on and switch the right one off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Savkic, are you able to describe this document, this document of 31 March 1992 that you're thinking of?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm referring to is the minutes from that Municipal Assembly session, or alternatively, there could have been a poll of citizens in the local communities, local communes belonging to Milici, as to whether they wish to unite into the Milici municipality. So you have these reports by local communes, and there's certainly a record of the session itself, the minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So prior to this decision and the session that you're referring to to form the Milici municipality, had there been any decisions taken at the republican level by the Assembly of the Serbian People to proclaim the municipality of Milici?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not. The initiative to set up the Milici Assembly dates back to the 1978 study. And there was a demand made to the initiative board of 1990 that the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica reject it, although the municipalities, all the local communes, both Muslim and Serb, from that municipality demanded that this municipality should separate. Any attempt to ascribe this attempt to that time period is absolutely wrong. I have a complaint from the chairman of the initiative board, and I'm talking about year 1979, why this municipality did not give its approval --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm going to have to stop you. But it is the case, obviously, that the history of any municipality is interesting, but we have to focus just on the issues that are relevant here and this historical record, unfortunately, is not relevant to the issues we're talking about today. Moving on to other matters dealing with the republican level. In May of 1992, did you receive the Official Gazette of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Milici?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, it would be best to ask that question of the president of the Municipal Assembly or the president of the Executive Council. Personally, I believe that in that period, although -- no. You'd better ask them. I had no insight into the work of the Municipal Assembly or the Executive Council, but if you're asking me, I didn't see that Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you aware that decisions taken at the republican level, or were you aware -- I'll ask you the question this way: Were decisions taken at the republican level implemented in the municipality of Milici in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to repeat this question once again: That question had better be put to the president of the Municipal Assembly and the president of the Executive Council. I cannot say one way or another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you know it, tell us whether you know it from your own observation or whether you know it because someone told you. If you don't know, please tell us as well, but to whom the question should have been addressed is -- Mr. Margetts will find someone else if you can't answer that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could turn to tab 5, and if the document there could have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 5, Your Honours, will be P1055.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. For the benefit of the parties and possibly the benefit of the witness, I brought the original of this document along because the copy in some respects is not as clear as it could be. So possibly if I could pass this first to the Trial Chamber and secondly to the Defence and finally to the witness. And, Your Honour, with the benefit of the original having been extracted from evidence, we obtained a revised translation, which we'll distribute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this is a decision taken by you as president of the Crisis Staff, and you'll see that the stamp there is the stamp of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, municipality of Milici, as the header on the document also depicts. And you'll see that the stamp at the top is marked 31 March 1992, and similarly the date in the preamble is 31 March 1992. Now, Mr. Savkic, this document in a number of ways contradicts the evidence you've given to this Trial Chamber. You've told the Trial Chamber that a Crisis Staff wasn't formed. You've told the Trial Chamber that if it was, you were never informed, and you never knew you were a member of the Crisis Staff. You've told the Trial Chamber that the Municipal Assembly was running the municipality, and this document quite clearly shows that the Crisis Staff in fact had authority. You have indicated to the Trial Chamber what you thought of the formation of Crisis Staffs by the Muslims without mentioning to the Trial Chamber that at that time you had already formed a Crisis Staff, you were president of that Crisis Staff, and it was operating. So in short, do you have any response to the inconsistency in this original document and your evidence?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, distinguished gentlemen. This document has its own background. First of all, it's obvious that they did everything well, but there's no signature of that president of the Crisis Staff called Tomislav Savkic. The forgery's all the greater because there is a seal, a stamp of the president of the Municipal Assembly, and it is numbered 1. The purpose of this document lies in another document that I have here, and it was needed by those gentlemen only in order to cover up the non-payment of taxes as costs of the greatest local company, the Boksit Company. So they were presenting or covering their non-payment of taxes in 1992 as allocations to the army. This was recovered in 1998, but the problem, Mr. Prosecutor, is that you are receiving documents to discredit me from criminals whom I have been persecuting all my life, and especially during the war in 1995 to 1998, when I was anti-constitutionally replaced from the post of president of Municipal Assembly. That is the only truth. All other versions are false. Even this stamp here does not correspond to the actual stamp from that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savkic. If -- so I take it that your response is again that there was no Crisis Staff, it didn't function, and that you consider this document is a forgery. That's correct? You consider this a forgery?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Distinguished gentlemen, I have stated before this Honourable Court that I am not informed whether that Crisis Staff ever existed, and I stand by that statement. I think all this can be subjected to expertise, and we can establish what the truth is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, if you -- in your last answer, when you say, "I'm not informed whether that Crisis Staff ever existed," is -- are you now referring to the Serb Crisis Staff of Milici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff of Milici, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I did not fully understand what this document was intended to cover up. I just didn't fully understand. This document says that the taxes on the turnover of the goods and services has been directed to the budget of the Milici municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dear sir, the Government of Republika Srpska, which was then called the government of the Serbian Republic Bosnia and Herzegovina, once passed a decree which states -- stated clearly that Municipal Assemblies can re-channel this tax by virtue of their own decisions to municipal budgets, because at that time municipalities financed everything, including the army. And it was said that at some point that municipalities should form Crisis Staffs whose competencies should include this as well. And I have a document from the time when the government asked the taxes to be paid. The President of the Executive Board had to submit, to attach one decision or another. He chose this one, and I can only guess at the reason. I suppose that in the period when this was ordered, from the 1st of January, 1992, until the 31st of December, there was neither a municipality or Assembly or various other authorities, so they zoomed in on the Crisis Staff. And if you allow me, I can find that document, a business arrangement between the Government of Republika Srpska and this particular company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd first please explain to me. I do understand from your answer that this document should cover up the non-payment of taxes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to cover up non-payment, actually, but to justify the allocations from that company to the army, to the police force, and the entire logistical base in that period. And all of this was actually justified, recognised until and including November. So they were given tax reliefs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take it step-by-step. The taxes on the turnover and services has been directed to the budget of Milici municipality. You say this document serves to justify the allocations from that company to the army, to the police force. What -- that company, which one is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that I have on me concerns the Boksit Company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So whether or not you have a document on it. So your answer is the Boksit Company, taxes paid per that company are now redirected to the budget of the Milici municipality through this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes and no. Yes, because of the wording. But in actual fact this tax was paid through allocations in kind, such as food. There is a system of barter lying behind it; allocations of oil, oil derivatives, et cetera. This was all calculated and compared to taxes due, and at the end of the year it turned out that, at the bottom line, the government should pay to the company another 100 million dinars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still not very -- not very clear, but, Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could move on -- and certainly that doesn't mean it's clear to the Prosecution either, but if we could move on to the next exhibit, and that's tab 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be tab 4, and tab 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Is previous Exhibit P64A, which is an excerpt from the 12th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly of 24 March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you have binder and tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I don't have anything more than P64. I'll attempt to get that. I think it's the footnotes of the Treanor report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed on the basis of the information you gave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, if I could refer you to this document, and in particular it's the part of this document which appears at page 40 before you, and you will see there's an eight-digit number at the top of the page that's stamped on the page, which is 00896896. Now, this is an extract of the proceedings of the Bosnian Serb Assembly of the 24th of March, 1992. And if you go down the page to the last paragraph, with the heading "Decision," and if you read that portion of the document to the end of the page, and that's sufficient. Yes. Mr. Savkic, have you read that part of that particular page, and do you see that that is a decision taken by the Assembly of the Serbian People on the verification of the decisions of municipal Assemblies on the proclamation of territories of the newly established Serb municipalities, and that includes Milici. Mr. Savkic, this contradicts your evidence as well. You said today, although you didn't say it in your evidence-in-chief, you said today that the municipal -- the municipality of Milici may have been proclaimed on the 31st of March, 1992. This decision clearly demonstrates it was proclaimed earlier. Secondly, you said this had nothing to do with decisions at a republican level. Well, this decision those that there was a proclamation of this municipality at the republican level. You also told the Trial Chamber at one stage of your evidence in chief that the municipal -- municipality of Milici, the Municipal Assembly of Milici, had no indicia of ethnicity. That's false as well. This decision demonstrates that it in fact was a Serb municipality. Do you have any explanation for the contradictions between the evidence you've given this Trial Chamber and this contemporaneous document?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear sirs, I will state unequivocally now: The Municipal Assembly of Milici - and I'm saying this officially now - was on the 31st of March, 1992, proclaimed, and I claim it will be confirmed by everyone from that negotiating team that worked a long time that our municipality adopted all these documents, including the protocol, without the knowledge of the authorities of Republika Srpska. And when I say without the knowledge, it's with the exception of this Bedjit [phoen], who probably made all that material available to them. And without the knowledge of the third rule authorities of Yugoslavia. I'm stating this responsibly. So as for who provided this information to the levels upstairs, I don't know, but it is not the first time that such documents are demonstrating that communication between the Government of Republika Srpska and the local authorities was not the best. But in view of the kind of times we were living in, that's no wonder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, regarding the communications between the Republika Srpska republican level and the regional level, I'd like to refer to the next page of this Assembly session, and in particular, I'd like to refer you to the paragraph that's about in the middle of the page and commences with the words: "Presidents of all SAOs should inform about the establishment of Serb municipalities," and I'd like to refer you to the -- not the next small sentence but next paragraph, which says: "The chairman -" that being Mr. Krajisnik - "explained, having said that all presidents of the autonomous regions had received instructions and that they were supposed to prepare and organise everything." So, Mr. Savkic, you see there that there's a reference to the work of the Serbian Autonomous Region presidents. Now, in your municipality, the Serbian Autonomous Region Assembly of Birac was the autonomous region Assembly that was responsible for Vlasenica and Milici. Now, in your evidence-in-chief you failed to refer to the existence of that Assembly, and you failed to refer to your involvement in it. And I'd like to refer to tab 41 of the Prosecution's exhibits, and that already has an exhibit number. And that is again P64A, and I understand that to be a footnote to Mr. Treanor's report. Mr. Savkic, if I could refer you first to page numbered 28, with the eight-digit stamp at the top 02919245, and you'll see this is the minutes of a meeting of the Assembly of the Autonomous District Birac held on 5 February 1992 in Milici. And then if I can get you to look over a number of pages, you will see that -- in fact, if you can go to page 33, which is marked at the top 02919250, you will see that there's a list of people who have been elected to working bodies of the Assembly. At section 4 you are marked as number 5. You have been elected to the political council of the Assembly of the Autonomous District Birac. Now, if I could now move to another exhibit, and that is the exhibit at tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Margetts has been going on for in excess of 25 lines. He has not asked the witness a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, do you want to put a question after you have confronted the witness with two documents, or is this document worth --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I think -- yes, Your Honour. Just in this instance it would be more efficient if I referred him to the other document as well, then asked him the question I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you're allowed to do so. Mr. Savkic -- but let me just -- I want to be sure that Mr. Savkic has found the portion where his name is mentioned, that is members elected to the political council. Have you found that, Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet, Your Honour. I didn't understand all that well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Savkic, semi-last page. At the very bottom of that page your name appears. And from the translation, the Chamber understands that that's a list of the members elected to the political council at the meeting of the Assembly of the Autonomous District Birac on the 5th of -- is it the 5th of February or the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The 5th of February, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5th of February, 1992. Have you found it? Yes? Mr. Margetts will now draw --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts will now draw your attention to another document but please keep this one in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And that's the document found at tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the minutes of the 1st session of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO, held on 18 February 1992. Mr. Savkic, if you look at the top of the first page of that document, you will see that this is the minutes of the Executive Council for SAO Birac. If you then look at the last line on the first page, continuing over to the second page, you will see that you, a part of a four-member team who were tasked to review the existing map of the ethnic region and to see a representative at the republican level by the name of Mr. Jovo Miskin. And then if I can refer you further down the page, you'll see that under the heading Conclusion, which appears towards -- just above the middle of the page, there are four steps set out for -- what it says is, it's -- these steps are set out: "In order to take over power in the area of the Birac SAO as efficiently as possible, it is necessary to take stock of the existing situation in the following spheres." The question I have for you, Mr. Savkic, is this: That having had a number of opportunities in the course of your examination-in-chief, and having been given an express opportunity to state all party, government, military positions you held, you failed to mention once your involvement in the Assembly of the SAO Birac, and you failed to mention this body at all whilst purporting in your evidence-in-chief to deal with the events in Vlasenica and Milici accurately. And so my question to you is this: Your evidence, Mr. Savkic, has been untrue and false in relation to your involvement in affairs in February 1992 in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, I'm hearing for the first time that a post or a function can be that deputy -- being a deputy can be a function, that being a member of a commission can also be a function, or a member of some board. According to what I believe, that was never so. Officials were always determined, and it is known who they are. What is just listed is something that never constituted a function and never will. It's true that this Assembly was held. That's beyond dispute. And as far as I can see, the first government session also was held. It's true that this government, this Executive Council, actually never fully functioned. There were some agreements to provide premises where they could actually meet to work, there were agreements about this and about that, but ultimately it all remained at the level of conclusions. Actually, the minute the decisions were made this body actually never became fully functional. That's how it was. The Birac SAO region - and everybody knows that - did not have any chances of becoming, and it never existed as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, we will address that matter in the course of another subject later on. Could I now turn to tab 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could we have the real response of Mr. Savkic. Mr. Savkic, what Mr. Margetts is confronting you with is that he says, well, what you told us about what your activities were, that's not complete, because already in February, you were involved in activities on the -- on this level in which you were tasked with reviewing the existing map of the ethnic region and -- so what he actually wants to confront you with is that in meetings where one was talking about in order to take over power, and that's February, that you did not give a full picture of what had happened in Milici because you left out your role in these activities in the Autonomous Birac reason -- region, Autonomous District. What's your comment on that? So let's not lose ourselves in semantics on whether it's a function or just a role or a position or -- that's not the core of the issue. The core of the issue is that where you gave a picture of others setting up Crisis Staffs and that you, as Mr. Margetts confronts you now with, were already busy with ethnic maps of the region, meetings where taking over of power was prepared or at least discussed. That's what Mr. Margetts would like know. At least, what the Chamber would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, as far as meetings are concerned regarding these matters - I'm speaking generally about the situation - we're talking about working meetings or party meetings, and here we see at the Assembly there were so many meetings that at such a turbulent time truly it was difficult for a man to remember all the details. If I am expected to recall where I was on each particular day and what I did, that then would create problems. When we're talking about this, these minutes and this agenda, I said that this government never came into being, never fully existed. That's evident. And the things that were adopted at that meeting that we, the four of us, should get in touch with Mr. Miskin, I don't know if any of these people were actually informed about it. One thing is certain, though: The four of us never actually met together. Even some of these people, Nego Jevtic, Mitar Tesic, I don't know if I ever actually met these people. They're completely unknown to me. Rajko Vidakovic. If that's the person that I think is here, I think I know him. But this person here, Nego Jevtic, please believe me when I say that I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hanoteau would have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dear sir, on table number 3 -- could we take a look at table -- at tab number 3. So at the conclusion, as the Prosecutor says, in English it says, "A four-member team of representatives of the region should be formed up and tasked to review the existing map..." and there's your name there. There's your name there, under that heading. So were you consulted? Were you told? Were you asked to be part of that team? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, definitely -- in particular before the meeting and definitely after the meeting, no. No, not to work with these people, two of whom I had never seen. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were never consulted to be part of that team? You were never asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is absolutely correct. I was never --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is it the first time that you noticed that you were part of that team, today? Is that the first time? Is that something that you're discovering right now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I am finding out now for the first time that I was a part of this team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could now turn to tab 7, Your Honour, and if that could have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 7, Your Honours, will be P1056.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you have before you a decision made by the president of the Assembly, Mile Lalovic, and it's dated 30 May 1992, and the preamble reads: "Based on the decision of the Serb Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina on the establishment of the army of the Serb Republic of BH (the Official Gazette number 6/92) and Article 27 of the statute of the Milici municipality, the Milici Municipal Assembly held on 30 May 1992 passed a decision on discontinuation of the Crisis Staff of the Milici municipality." The first thing is this, Mr. Savkic: Is that you didn't say whether or not you knew whether decisions of the republican level were implemented in Milici. Do you see now that they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Why does this document help with that question? Surely my learned friend needs to establish some groundwork whether the witness accepts the veracity of the document, he's ever seen it before, whether he can comment on it, just the same way that the Defence have repeatedly been told they have to do that with documents they put before witnesses. The exact same thing applies, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, in view of the objection, could you please lay the relevant groundwork.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I may just -- I may just withdraw that area of inquiry and proceed to other matters which arise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, can you refer to paragraph 2 of this decision. It states there: "Instead of the Crisis Staff, the Military Command of the Milici Municipality and the Wartime Presidency of the Milici Municipality have been established." Now, Mr. Savkic, that contradicts the evidence that you've given this Trial Chamber. The evidence you gave this Trial Chamber on a number of occasions was that it was the Municipal Assembly and the Executive Board that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, I think you were invited to lay the -- the relevant groundwork, and it seems that you just continue, or is that the wrong understanding of your approach?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's correct. That's what I did. I guess I should then respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The situation is as follows, Your Honour: We have a number of documents and the Prosecutor is satisfied of their authenticity --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Objection to that comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, tab 7. Have you ever seen that document in your life before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I've never seen this document before, but -- but what I said regarding the first decision stands. You can see that this is the stamp of the president of the Assembly. I'm now reading for the first time this decision. Please, Article 2: Instead of the Crisis Staff, the military command of the Milici municipality is being formed. If we really look at the reality, until the 19th of May, the 19th of May, 1992, there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, nothing really corresponds to -- I'm seeing this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know who Lalovic Mile is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mile Lalovic is the president of the Municipal Assembly, the first president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember the signature of Lalovic Mile on this document -- do you recognise the signature of Lalovic Mile on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure if that's his signature, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said something --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said something about the stamp. You said you can see that this is the stamp of the president of the Assembly. What did you mean to say by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I meant was when we were talking about the Crisis Staff, the decision regarding the taxes, the decision of the Crisis Staff on taxes, this is the confirmation that the stamp on that document is the stamp of the president of the Municipal Assembly. We have the whole background, which I already suggested to you. I suggested what the main purpose was. The main purpose was to have the Boksit Company avoid paying taxes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does the stamp say? Does it say "The Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, opstina Milici"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the stamp as such, if you say that stamp appears once on a decision which is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and another time that it is a decision of the Municipal Assembly, the stamp in itself doesn't give any clue as to whether it's either Crisis Staff or Municipal Assembly, or perhaps even both, if one considers them both to be part of the opstina of Milici. Is this a correct conclusion, or would you draw my attention to any other aspect of these stamps which would contradict what seems, in my view, to be the obvious.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you see here that there's a stamp here and also the name of the president of the municipality. The document which was used to cover the non-payment of taxes, there is no signature there. So it seems that that person is me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that signature is not the same as stamps. The stamps you have seen before and this stamp -- that, is the stamp on the text decision and this stamp, do you consider those to be the same stamps or do you see any difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely number one. In both the stamps it's the stamp of the president of the Assembly. There is no need to say that until that time the gentleman worked at the Boksit Company too. The whole purpose, again, is to evade paying taxes. That's why it was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you say this is the stamp of the president of the Assembly, which seems to support the origin of this document to be the Assembly. On that basis and not having given any decision, Mr. Margetts, on the authenticity of this document, you may put further questions to the witness as to the content, of course within the limits of his own knowledge, and please keep in mind it is the first time he sees this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the second paragraph accurately sets out the municipal authorities in 1992. That is as follows: In April and May of 1992, or prior -- let's say this: Prior to the 30th of May, 1992, the Crisis Staff was the municipal authority, and subsequent to the 30th of May, 1992, the military command and the wartime Presidency of Milici was the municipal authority, and your evidence that it was the Municipal Assembly is false; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying again that the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Milici did not exist because there was nobody to constitute such a body. And please, we are here because of the truth. So for the sake of truth, we need to see the minutes of all the Municipal Assembly sessions and the sessions of the Executive Board of the Milici Municipal Assembly from the 31st of March until the 30th of May, 1991, and then we will have a clear picture of what the Municipal Assembly was doing and what was the Crisis Staff doing. I can say that the background of all that is written here. I can tell you what the background is if the Court wishes to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have specific knowledge on the -- especially then paragraph 2, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but surely the question is very straightforward. The question Mr. Margetts is asking is does the witness accept what is said in paragraph 2 of this document. It's as straightforward as that and the witness needs to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness did that. The witness said that it couldn't be true because the Crisis Staff never existed, and now he wants to explain to us the background. He's invited to do so if he has any specific knowledge on it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, I think that a couple of days before - perhaps on that day - the president of the republic abolished the Crisis Staffs. This gentleman here, known as a bureaucrat, probably proposed to the National Assembly -- no, not the National Assembly but the Municipal Assembly -- made the proposal to the Municipal Assembly, and it decided to abolish something that never actually existed, unless he wanted to conceal or keep from knowledge that evasion of taxes which happened when he was president. This Article 2 also is illogical to the extent that "the military command" is a term that was actually never used. It was always referred to in that period as "the command of the town" or "the staff of the Territorial Defence." Both terms were used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, while explaining the document, you say, as a matter of fact, that because there was a decision on a higher level that Crisis Staffs should be abolished, that even where there was no Crisis Staff it was abolished just following the instructions, I would say blindly, without thinking about it, and you say that it also becomes apparent if you use the language used here, which is not -- okay. That's a clear answer. Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I note the time. I would be presenting another exhibit and wouldn't be finished within the next minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break until ten minutes past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I receive the French translation of my own words in English for a second, but I take it that we're back on English and on channel 4. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two documents I'd like to present, and they both need exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The first document I'll be referring to is a document dated 27 May 1992, and the second is one dated 31 May 1992. And the Defence already has a copy of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you provide the witness with a copy. And Mr. Registrar, that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first document, dated 27 May, 1992, Your Honours, will be P1057; and other one, dated 31 May 1992, will be P1058, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you're looking at the document which is P1057, which is a document dated 27 May 1992, and is a report of the duty officer to the commander of the police station of Milici. I don't expect that you would have received this, given it's addressed to Mr. Bjelanovic; however, if your friend Mr. Bjelanovic gave it to you or you saw it otherwise, could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether or not you've seen it.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Savkic. If you could look at the second part of the report, which is titled "Parties." And it refers to the incident when the convoy of trucks was attacked, which you've referred to. The last two sentences read as follows: "The attack took place in Konjevic Polje," and the last sentence says: "The Milici Crisis Staff was informed of the attack." Mr. Savkic, this document contradicts your evidence that the Milici Crisis Staff was not functioning, and this document shows, in fact, that the Milici Crisis Staff was being informed of the events in the terrain; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, although it's the third time I'm saying this, I have to repeat it. Obviously the Prosecutor is not listening to what I'm saying. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, it is -- the Prosecutor is entitled, if he finds other documents in which the existence or the functioning of a Crisis Staff in his view is expressed, to confront you with that, and you should then refrain from -- say that it doesn't change your answer or that it did not exist or whether it's a forgery of -- or whether the author of this document is an idiot, but please give an answer to his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've just read this, but Milovan Kresimir, I don't know which Milovan is meant. Maybe the duty officer of the public security station. But in fact, that is not in issue. I have to tell you this: Very often -- I told you how many times the staff was renamed: Staff of the army, staff of the battalion, staff of the Territorial Defence, city staff, command of the city, et cetera, et cetera. It's possible that in all this ignorance precisely this military authority is named here Crisis Staff. That's a possibility, because the person who wrote this is a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'd like to refer you to the next document, which is P1058. It's dated the 31st of May, 1992. That again is a report to Mr. Rade Bjelanovic, the commander of the police station, and I refer you to the part that mentions your name, and it's the last part of the report. It says: "Tomo Savkic was escorted by a patrol composed of M. Milosevic, G. Lalovic and R. Saric." And it states that the patrol left at 2200, direction of Milici-Vlasenica. The reference to "M. Milosevic" is a reference to the policeman stationed at the Milici police station, Milomir Milosevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All the three policemen are from Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Milomir Milosevic was a subordinate of Mr. Rade Bjelanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I've finished with that document. Now, the takeover of the town of Vlasenica occurred on the 20th of April, 1992, and that takeover was performed by the forces of the Yugoslav army and the formed unit that was coordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to refer to the document that's at tab 6. And if that could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 6 has no number yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1059, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this is a report setting out the history of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade sent by commander Major Mile Kosoric to the Drina Corps command. And you can see in the first paragraph it reads as follows: "On 20 April 1992 the forces of the Yugoslav Army and the formed unit coordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff liberated the town of Vlasenica." It then goes on to describe other activities of the SDS Crisis Staff and the history of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade. It is correct, isn't it, that the takeover was performed by the JNA together with the unit that was coordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely not correct. It's not true. This heading here, combined with the contents below serves I don't know what purpose. I don't know to speak about the setting up of all this, because you can see from the dates that it's from the 19th of May onwards how the units were formed after that date. Everybody understands that. Let me comment on the first part. On the 20th of April, 1992, the forces of the Yugoslav army and the formed unit led by the SDS Crisis Staff liberated the town of Vlasenica. What I know is this: I described precisely how Vlasenica was taken over and what preceded that event. I have in front of me an original document -- or, rather, a copy of the original document, entitled "Report of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence of Vlasenica," addressed to the Main Staff of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and this document will fully confirm what I said at the time, and I will kindly ask the distinguished Judges, because this is a very important document not only confirming what I said in my testimony but also one that speaks to the scenario of genocidal cleansing of those three municipalities. And if the Honourable Court allows me, I will explain it later. But as for this passage here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you shown this document to Defence counsel with whom you have spoken before the beginning of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. But this document and another one I left aside precisely for the cross-examination, because I expected the Prosecutor to try to discredit me as a person and as a witness, and I wanted to keep this in store to -- to show who actually perpetrated all the evil in Vlasenica. I hope -- I don't know what the procedures are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. We have a submission on what the procedures are. Obviously, it would be our position that at this stage we'd like the witness to answer our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: How he proceeds in re-examination is a matter for him -- well, for his Defence counsel, but this doesn't constitute an answer to my question. This constitutes an attempt to introduce new evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, an attempt to introduce no evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: "The Defence counsel" rather than "his Defence counsel." I'm sorry to be pedantic, but it's an important point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would have corrected these words as well if I were in Mr. Josse's position. At the same time, the witness offers new material, which seems to be unknown to both parties and which might be of importance to better understand his testimony and also perhaps to better appreciate what you try to establish at this moment, that is that the documents give a different version of the events if we compare it with the testimony of this witness. Would you mind to give a copy of that document, which I take it is in your own language? Is that correct? Would you please be so kind to give a copy at the end of this hearing to the registrar so that he can make copies for the parties so that the parties can see whether it's of any use for them, and the Chamber will try to explore and see whether this is evidence which is of such importance that we should call it ourselves. So -- then you get back the document once we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm only interrupting, Your Honour, because I can assure the Court I will deal with this in re-examination. So I wasn't clear when Your Honour used the word "hearing" what Your Honour meant. I assumed at the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Because -- thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, we may have submissions to make as to whether it's an appropriate matter to be dealt with in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We do not know yet what the document is, but the witness raises the issue of the existence of this document in relation to one of your questions, and we'll see to what extent it's proper to deal with it in re-examination. At least, Mr. Margetts, you know that if the Chamber is aware of what the document is, the Chamber is not bound by the question whether it is examination in chief or re-examination. We'd like to receive that later on. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in 1992 in Vlasenica, there was a War Presidency of the Milici municipality that you failed to tell this Trial Chamber about, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Presidency do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The War Presidency of Milici municipality.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to assert once again. If this existed, then the president of the Municipal Assembly of Milici should have known about this. I didn't know about that Presidency, because I know that the Assembly and the Executive Council were operational. Both sat in their offices and all citizens who had any affairs to settle with them went to see one or the other. And of course they dealt in everyday life with the rest of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could refer to tab 16 and if that could be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 16, Your Honour, would be P1060.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, as you can see, this document is on the letterhead of the Republika Srpska, Milici Municipality War Presidency, and it's stamped as the creation of the War Presidency. You can also see that your good friend, confidant, Radomir Bjelanovic is a member of this Presidency as represented at paragraph 6 and on the first page. Having seen this document, Mr. Savkic, do you now agree that your evidence was incorrect and there was a War Presidency that was operational in Milici municipality?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you see, in this Presidency, if it existed, you don't see name. That's one thing. Another thing: I don't see any reason why this person Mile Lalovic, president of the Presidency, would inform the commander, the 8th of December, the commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion, that the War Presidency was being established. I am saying once again: If it existed, I never attended their sessions, and I am seeing these names for the first time. Let me have a look at this 8th December thing. Maybe there was some heavy combat going on in that period. But I don't want to comment on something I have no knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, if I could refer you to page 3 of the document and to the last -- the last seven lines of the major paragraph on page 3. And there was discussion about the competence of the garrison commander, and the minutes record that the commander, who they refer to as Milenko Petkovic, "acts like a demagogue in the army, so in order to avoid any serious consequences, our suggestion is that he be relieved of his duties and that Captain Zoran Pantic be appointed in his place ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you referring to English, the English page, or to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I only referred to the B/C/S page. In the English page, the portion I'm reading from is the bottom two lines of page 3 and proceeding over to the continuation of that paragraph and to the end of the paragraph on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're reading from item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'm reading --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no. Sorry, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, Your Honour. It's item 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's item 2 but the last -- well, starting approximately ten lines from the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's item 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the item. Yes. I think we've found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm particularly concerned with the last two lines of page 3 and the four lines that appear at the top of page 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It records: "If there are any problems with Pantic's appointment, our suggestion is that the present commanders of the battalion, Tomislav Savkic and Radomir Dzinkic, reserve captains, be appointed, as known officers and fighters." It's correct at that time, Mr. Savkic, isn't it, that you'd been appointed to the command of the Milici Battalion, and you were known in battle as a good fighter.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you at all. I told you that from the 1st November, 1992, onwards, I was commander of the battalion. This here is dated the 8th of December. That's 38 days later. By that time, I was already commander. I don't see the point. If you allow me, I would like to read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer, therefore, is simple: "Yes, I was commander of the battalion," and then we'll wait what the next question will be. Yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Savkic, the reason that you're referred to as a good officer and a fighter and the reason that you were appointed commander of the battalion is because you were engaged in the military operations that took place to clear the access roads between Milici and Zvornik and Milici and Bratunac; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It doesn't say he was a good officer and a good fighter. It says he was a known officer and a fighter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was always my understanding of the English language that if you're saying he's a known pianist that it's usually not because he's playing so bad, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I wouldn't accept that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then my understanding of the English language falls short. Would you please confront the witness with being a known fighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be our submission that your understanding of the English language is perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not further explore the differences between the English and -- as it is spoken in different parts of the world. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the reason that you were a known officer and fighter and you were appointed to the position of the commander of the Milici Battalion was that you had been engaged in the military operations to clear the access roads between Milici and the two eastern cities of Zvornik and Bratunac; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely untrue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, it doesn't help very much to put two questions in one, because if the response is in the negative -- why not first ask the witness whether he was engaged in the military operations you mentioned; and then if you're interested to know whether that is why he was called a known fighter, I don't know whether that's -- could be, but that's at least a different question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you were involved in the military operations to clear the access roads between Milici and Zvornik and Bratunac, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could move to the next tab, which is tab 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, if I may, Mr. Witness, please. If I could have -- I just want know something. Were you aware of the problems with Milenko Petrovic, the commander of the Milici garrison? It says he shouldn't continue being tasked with his job. Did you know about this? Was that a problem? Were you aware of that -- of that problem with Milenko Petrovic and the way he behaved? Milenko Petkovic. I want "yes" or "no" as an answer. Were you aware of the problem with this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was, but very little, and I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were aware. You were aware.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I won't proceed now to the tab I earlier indicated. I'll proceed instead to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, I thought it was the habit of the Chamber that if a witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I made a note that the witness said it's very important and what it was about, so that we can come to it -- back to it at a later stage, depending on how testimony develops, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry. I'll just ask one question prior to referring to the next exhibit, and I apologise for various directions I've proceeded in in the last few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, as at January 1993, you had over 700 men under your command, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January 1993, I had not 700. I had more than 700. I think it was around 900 people under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll refer to the next exhibit, and that is the exhibit at tab 19. Now, Your Honour, Mr. Josse has been good enough to tell us that -- to alert us to an error in the translation. Unfortunately, we haven't been able to rectify that prior to presenting this document before the Trial Chamber, and it's not one we wish to read out on the record, but if we could tell Your Honour where this error is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And tell you that -- and inform the Chamber that the parties have agreed that this particular portion be deleted. So before presenting this to the witness, I'd just like to refer to that. And Your Honours have before you this document which is dated 21 August 1995. You will see in paragraph 2, which is on the second page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- at -- in -- on the third line of that paragraph there is something which is behind -- there are four words behind a back slash and then there is a forward slash, and it is the back slash, the four words, and the forward slash that we would like struck from this translation and our preferred way to proceed, just for efficiency, would be that a line be ruled through that so that it is deleted from this translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand that it is because it does not appear in the original language?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore it's just the four words, the first starting with the D and the fourth ending with an S, which should be taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Then the registrar is instructed to -- or if you -- do you have the -- Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if we could have a number for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. If we could have a number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 19, Your Honours, will be P1061.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you have before you a document signed by you as president of the War Presidency of Milici.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document that I signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Despite ample opportunity, you have not been fully truthful with the Trial Chamber, and this document demonstrates that. You were the president of the War Presidency of Milici municipality, and you failed to inform the Trial Chamber of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're talking about the 18th of August, 1995. It's very important to stress -- actually, the explanation is very simple. On the 5th of August, with the attack of the Croatian army on the Knin-Krajina, there was a decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If I could stop the witness there. I'm just referring specifically to whether or not he occupied that position. If the answer's yes, then that's adequate for my purposes. Or if the answer is no. Whatever his answer is, it's a simple yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness pointed at the date, or at least at a date, because I see two dates. Were you president of the War Presidency of Milici municipality in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, after Croatia's attack on Krajina -- yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the first -- the first question I'd like you to answer is whether you were president of the -- of the War Presidency in 1995. So that now has been -- that's now part of your testimony. If -- yes. It's clear. We're talking about 1995. Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the map which is at tab 17 could be given a number and presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 17 will be P1062.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you have before you a map of an area of Eastern Bosnia which incorporates almost the top of the municipality of Zvornik, and Pale is noted down in the left corner of the map. There are six villages marked in red and relatively large type face, and those villages are Vlasenica, Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Milici, Srebrenica, and Zepa. It is the fact, isn't it, Mr. Savkic, that the Muslims in 1992, from around April 1992, left Vlasenica in various directions, that enclaves were formed in Cerska and Konjevic Polje. It's also correct that after various military operations, they left the enclaves of Cerska and Konjevic Polje in around March of 1993, and they then occupied Srebrenica before they left Srebrenica following the attack which commenced on the 12th of July 1995. That is the correct description of the movement of the Muslim population through the enclaves and eventually from the Srebrenica enclave; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part is absolutely incorrect. That is already historically known. The history is known, that when we're talking about the Cerska enclave, for the most part that's what you call Konjevic Polje, but it's actually much broader than that. And all of that is via Kamenica, which is also an enclave. And they all went to Kalesija or, rather, Tuzla. A very small number of members of the armed formations from Cerska, from this part, went to Srebrenica. Before that, I want to add that the complete civilian population took this road that I mentioned to Kalesija, or Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, can you describe to -- Mr. Savkic, the -- the members of the defence units, including the units that you were involved with in August 1992, those soldiers that were stationed in Milici and the surrounding municipalities of Sekovici and Zvornik, knew of the conditions in the enclave of Cerska, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
